nodes.name: Locale is available in early access. It is not generally…
nodes.text: Locale is available in early access. It is not generally available and not sold as a standalone product. This essay describes how it works and the principles behind it; details may still change, and What’s new? will say when they do.

nodes.name: A product with a web app, an iOS app and an Android app…
nodes.text: A product with a web app, an iOS app and an Android app usually has three translation catalogs in three formats. They share most of their terminology and some of their strings, but each also has text of its own. Teams end up copying glossaries between repositories and hoping they stay in sync.

nodes.name: Locale is built around the same workspace, product and…
nodes.text: Locale is built around the same workspace, product and project structure as the rest of NullDull. A project keeps its own languages, formats and configuration. Shared context, such as a product-wide glossary, is linked explicitly and individually authorized. Unrelated projects’ translations are never silently pooled.

nodes.name: The unit of work is a translation key with its values per…
nodes.text: The unit of work is a translation key with its values per language. Each key has one explicit status: draft, needs review or approved. Values use typed `{{name}}` variables declared on the key, and plural forms follow the language’s rules. A save with an undeclared or malformed placeholder is rejected rather than shipped broken.

nodes.name: Every change to a key is versioned, with atomic updates…
nodes.text: Every change to a key is versioned, with atomic updates per language and request receipts, so concurrent editors and agents don’t overwrite each other’s work. Completeness is derived from the values rather than stored, so a key that is missing a language always shows it, wherever it was edited.

nodes.name: Locale converts one canonical catalog to and from the…
nodes.text: Locale converts one canonical catalog to and from the formats apps actually use: JSON, World, Xcode String Catalogs, Xcode `.strings` and `.stringsdict`, and Android `strings.xml`. A format either carries a feature—plurals, variables, status, names—or fails explicitly. It never drops something quietly.

nodes.name: Import and export use the same operations in the browser,…
nodes.text: Import and export use the same operations in the browser, the HTTP API, MCP and the CLI, with the same permissions. A private workspace API key with read-only Locale export access lets a build pipeline fetch catalogs without a person’s session.

nodes.name: Machine translation is useful and imperfect, so Locale…
nodes.text: Machine translation is useful and imperfect, so Locale makes its output visible. AI-written values are saved as needing review, never as approved, and only people in the browser can mark a value approved. Agents can never approve translations, and an agent’s change to an approved value sends it back to review.

nodes.name: Teams can attach Memory files they can read—a style guide,…
nodes.text: Teams can attach Memory files they can read—a style guide, a terminology note—as translation guidelines, in priority order. Attaching one is a deliberate browser action, because translations shaped by a guideline become visible to everyone with Locale access at that location. Attaching a guideline never grants anyone access to the Memory file itself.

nodes.name: Automatic translation follows the same principle. It is a…
nodes.text: Automatic translation follows the same principle. It is a per-location setting, off by default. When a manager turns it on, new source text queues its empty languages for AI fill as the person who wrote it; edits to existing text never trigger it, and failures wait for an explicit retry instead of running again on their own.
